alyssa: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-affinity change i'm seeing p95 tail spikes for small-seq workloads (<=64). looks tied to FlashAttention switching when paged-KV misses happen. attaching short profile dump below.

runtime-bot: profiler run 1800123456: batcher.queue_depth=120, avg_batch_size=8, flash_runs=73, fallback_runs=19, paged_kv_page_faults=42, p95_latency_ms=48.3

jorge: can you paste the profiler command? want to grab same slice.

alyssa: run `perfdump --window=2026-03-16T22:00:00Z..2026-03-16T22:10:00Z --tag=batching,kv,kernel` — i filtered for requests with seq_len<=64 and kv_pages_accessed>0. key lines:

```
kernel=flashattention seq=32 gpu_time_ms=0.9 overhead_ms=3.8 launch_count=120
kernel=std_matmul     seq=32 gpu_time_ms=1.4 overhead_ms=1.1 launch_count=30
kv_page_faults=42 total_kv_prefetch=6 average_prefetch_latency_ms=6.2
p95_total_ms=48.3 p50_total_ms=12.1
```

maya: interesting — flash gpu_time is lower but overhead and page-faults blow up when KV paging occurs. that overhead seems to be killing tail since flash launches more often for those seq lengths.

devon: so root cause: kernel selection picks flash for small seq, but flash has worse amortized kernel-launch+kv-miss overhead because it creates more short-lived kernels? could also be memory access pattern with paged-kv.

jorge: two quick heuristics to try:
- prefer std_matmul for seq<=32 when paged_kv_page_faults>threshold
- add dynamic priority aging so older requests with partial prefixes get coalesced into earlier batches
- lower token_budget_target from 2048 to 1024 for queues with high page-fault rate (reduce fragmentation)

alyssa: +1. also want to try prefetching KV pages for requests that predictably touch the same pages (session affinity). cheap prefetch seems to reduce faults in synthetic runs.

perfbot: experiment suggestion #1: A/B with kernel affinity override: group id=kv-heavy -> forced kernel=std_matmul. Measure p95 and throughput for 24h. expected: p95 drop for small seq, small throughput regression for long seq.

maya: another option: change continuous-batcher to bias by "effective token cost" where flash has extra fixed overhead weight when paged_kv_miss_rate>0. i.e. cost = tokens + fixed_overhead*miss_rate. batcher then prefers to coalesce more small-seq into fewer kernels.

alyssa: i sketched config keys:
```
batcher.dynamic_token_budget = 1024
batcher.kernel_overhead_weight.flash = 4.0
batcher.kernel_overhead_weight.std = 1.0
queue.age_threshold_ms = 8
queue.prefetch_kv=true
```

devon: plan of action:
1) implement kernel_overhead_weight + dynamic token budget flag (dev branch)
2) run perf A/B across 20 canary machines with synthetic mix (20% kv-heavy small-seq)
3) collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, gpu_util, kv_page_faults
4) if p95 improves >20% and throughput drops <5% -> roll canary to 10% prod

jorge: one gotcha — ensure paging metrics are from the same driver build. last week we had a subtle driver change that changed page fault accounting; make sure perfbot pulls same driver tag.

maya: do we have an experiment harness command? i can wire up a scenario generator.

alyssa: use `batcher-experiment --mix=small_seq_kv:0.2,default:0.8 --duration=2h --collect=latency,gpu,kv` — i've got a harness branch linked in my PR.

perfbot: short checklist for the run:
- enable `batcher.kernel_overhead_weight` (dev flag)
- set `batcher.dynamic_token_budget=1024` on canaries
- run harness with trace-id prefix `kv-flash-test-180012`
- collect traces and export to /perf/experiments/180012_kv_flash

devon: one more caution: rollout policy must have automatic rollback if p99 increases or error rate increases >0.2%. add a guard in rollout config.

alyssa: i'll push the kernel_overhead_weight patch and a test that simulates paged-kv misses. will post PR link here.

jorge: thanks — after the run we should also add a short kernel-selection unit test that asserts we pick std for seq<=16 with high page-fault rates.

maya: awesome. if the week goes well we should fold this heuristic into the global model profile so Dedicated customers get the same stability.

runtime-bot: noted new experiment scheduled by alyssa: id=180012_kv_flash, start=2026-03-17T03:00:00Z, canaries=20, expected_duration=2h. will report when complete.

alyssa: thanks all, i'll update this thread with PR + early graphs when the canary finishes. :thumbsup:
